items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I'm thinking of Lester Young, and Basie had a great tenor player named Herschel Evans... they left Pres with his crooked neck saxophone.

ctx.x: Oh, Pres was in that band. That was a great band. And when Count took it over. He wanted to come to Chicago, and Fletcher was instrumental in getting Count in the Grand Terrace. Buck Clayton, the trumpet player, was in that band --Harry and Sweets Edison. Oh, man, those are legends, those guys. And when Fletcher went out on the road, Ed Fox's Grand Terrace was the popular club in Chicago, and Fletcher recommended Basie to this gentleman that owned the club, and went in there and did a terrific Basie was a man…

And I made a couple of original things for Basie, and I don't know if he recorded them or not, but I'd heard that band, and it was easy to write, you know, and he often told me, he says, 'If you have anything good that you think is good, and you know my style, he said, send it on in to the office.
